concepts.prompt: Create a single landscape 16:9 painted 2D Zoe Force game concept, highly detailed and production-oriented. Reference image 1 is the ORIGINAL game's layout and information to preserve. Reference image 2 is the APPROVED-FOR-EXPLORATION visual family to match: use its bone-and-black-metal biomechanical cathedral architecture, muted ivory/charcoal/oxblood palette, cyan player accents and red/orange threats. H.R. Giger meets Life Force, with Contra: Shattered Soldier's dense weapon/machinery detail adapted into flat illustrated 2D layers. Smooth painted edges, no voxel blocks and no pixel grid. Keep playable elements immediately legible. This is a concept mockup for review, not an implemented screenshot. No watermark or extra explanatory captions. Asset type: title screen and main menu concept. Preserve the original screen's hierarchy and five menu choices. A dark biomechanical cathedral corridor frames an intentionally calm, opaque central menu area. Elegant etched bone-metal game logo reading exactly "ZOE FORCE", with subtitle "SIX TERROR ZONES". Beneath it: "THE YEAR IS ALWAYS NOW. THE FUTURE IS LATE." and "PILOT 1". Five generously separated, precisely readable menu rows: "START GAME", "STAGE SELECT", "RECORDS", "PROFILES", "OPTIONS". START GAME is visibly selected with a luminous ivory border, subtle oxblood fill and small mechanical chevrons. All labels in crisp restrained sci-fi lettering, high contrast; no ornate anatomy behind letters. Put the little player fighter to screen-left of the selected menu row, nose pointing screen-right (increasing X), matching the reference. Lower footer: "Z FIRE   X POWER-UP   ARROWS MOVE", "M — FIRE MODE: MANUAL", "HI 0000000". Preserve the existing small bottom game HUD as a compact bone-metal instrumentation strip: score, five upgrade slots SPEED/MISSILE/LASER/OPTION/FORCE, and three ship-life icons. Do not add a health bar, shop, online options, or new gameplay promises. Background detailed along outer edges, subdued behind menus. The visual result should feel polished and navigable, not like a busy movie poster.

No labels floating over gameplay, no decorative machinery obstructing the clear flight lane.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single widescreen 16:9 painted 2D gameplay concept for Zoe Force, Stage 1 BIO-CATHEDRAL. The attached original screenshot is a composition and gameplay-layout reference, not an art-style reference. Re-conceptualize its simple pixel art into an exceptionally detailed, hand-painted 2D scrolling-shooter frame. Art direction: H.R. Giger-inspired biomechanical architecture meets Life Force's organic corridor, with the dense surface and weapon detail of Contra: Shattered Soldier translated into illustrated 2D. No voxel blocks, no pixel-art grid, no perspective gameplay camera. Preserve the original side-on screen coordinates: small player ship near screen-left at approximately 16% X and 47% Y, nose pointing screen-right (increasing X); broad unobstructed flight lane; ceiling and floor boundaries follow the reference; a small formation of enemies on screen-right. Build the upper and lower corridor walls from fused bone-metal ribs, dark arterial cables, interlocking vertebrae, subtle living tissue, inset vents, and wet oxidized surfaces. Receding architectural layers stay behind the flight lane and create atmospheric depth without solid objects in the navigable space. Ship: sleek bone-white armored fighter, visible side profile and cyan engine detail, clear silhouette, three pale cyan laser beams traveling horizontally screen-right, small orange missile exhausts and restrained translucent shield. Enemies are unmistakably separate from scenery, threatening small biomechanical craft. Palette: charcoal and antique ivory, restrained dark oxblood tissue and blue-gray metal, small cyan player-fire accents, warm red/orange threats. Dramatic directed lighting, rich fine texture concentrated along the solid corridor edges, low-contrast background behind bullets. Smoothly painted sprite edges, mostly 2D layers with tasteful depth. Preserve a narrow dark bottom strip for a separate HUD concept; do not add text, labels, a logo, or a watermark. This is a production-oriented gameplay mockup, not a poster: keep every ship, bullet, and safe-space boundary instantly readable.
